title: The Mirrored Study Where Books Teach Themselves

features.name: the-facing-mirrors
features.desc-on-touch: Two mirrors angled so they reflect each other forever, each holding a reader who is learning that reading is an angle of light, not a sequence of words.

features.name: the-library-rows
features.desc-on-touch: Each spine a position in a conversation that books have learned to have without human hands turning pages. The shelves teach themselves their own order.

features.name: margin-annotation
features.desc-on-touch: A note left in a margin, written by a reader so attentive to light that they forgot to read the text. The note teaches the book something it didn't know about itself.

features.name: the-study-s-angle
features.desc-on-touch: The slant of afternoon light through the window, teaching both readers that everything they're reading is a surface learning how to cast a shadow.

inscription: two readers in the same room learning that reading is about the angle of light, not the text

reverie.title: REVERIE — study where light teaches
narr: You sit across from her in the study, both reading.
The light moves. Neither of you turns a page.
She's learning that the angle of afternoon matters
more than the words. So are you. The shelf watches
you both forgetting what the books were meant to say.
The room teaches you both the same lesson: reading
